title: Crikvenica With a Dog 2027: Beaches, Rules, Costs
metaDescription: Crikvenica with a dog: Podvorska dog beach, hotel pet fees from €20, ferries, heat, vets and EU pet passport rules, plus a clear verdict for 2027.
content:
## Dog Beaches in Crikvenica: Podvorska and Monty's Dog Beach & Bar

Crikvenica has an official dog beach, Podvorska, in the small harbour (lučica) Podvorska, close to the town centre. It opened in July 2010, and entry is free. The beach is gravel, about 170 m long and 20 m wide (roughly 3,400 m²). It has changing cabins, showers, benches, bins and a shower reserved for dogs. Sunbeds and umbrellas can be rented.

The beach bar, Monty's Dog Beach & Bar, calls itself the first dog café in Croatia. The dog menu includes dog ice cream, dog beer, herbal teas, chips and cake. Owners get cocktails and coffee. Rules of conduct are posted on a board at the entrance, and dogs move freely. In summer the beach runs events such as a dog swimming contest and puppy yoga. A beach bar with the same name and owners operates on the island of Rab.

Bring a leash for the walk there, one or two water bowls, a blanket or shade for the dog, and food. Dog food is also sold locally.

## Are Dogs Allowed on Other Beaches in Croatia?

In most of Croatia, dogs are not allowed on regular municipal and hotel beaches. Official dog beaches are signed separately. The usual reasons are hygiene rules and local by-laws. Check the sign at the entrance, because rules differ between towns. In Crikvenica the practical answer is simple: swim your dog at Podvorska, and avoid the main town beaches in season.

Outside the bathing season, leashed dogs on the promenade and rocky shore are generally tolerated. Do not assume the same on beaches with lifeguards or sunbed concessions.

## Old Town, Promenades and Walks

Crikvenica is a seaside resort with a long promenade rather than a walled old town. Leashed dogs are normal on the waterfront paths. Several coastal paths suit dog walks, including the Kačjak–Perhati trail between Dramalj and Jadranovo. On hot days walk before 9:00 or after 18:00, because the asphalt and stone get very hot.

## Restaurants and Cafés

Terraces on the Croatian coast usually accept dogs on a leash, and many bring a water bowl without being asked. Indoor dining is at the owner's discretion, and many restaurants refuse dogs inside. Ask before sitting down. Monty's Dog Beach & Bar is the one place where the dog is the main guest.

## National Parks, Ferries and Catamarans

Rules for national parks differ by park, and some, including Plitvice Lakes, restrict dogs heavily. Check the park's own rules before driving. Close to Crikvenica, the Kvarner islands are a day-trip option. Car ferries generally accept dogs, usually on a leash or muzzle and on the open deck or in the car, while passenger catamarans set their own conditions, so confirm with the operator when buying a ticket. Fares for dogs are normally small or free, but they vary by operator.

## What Accommodation Charges for a Dog

Pet fees in Crikvenica run in two tiers:

- **Hotels:** Hotel Crikvenica charges €20 per pet per day (dogs and cats, one pet, up to about 15 kg, certain rooms only). Hotel Omorika charges €25 per pet per night and provides bowls. Hotel Slaven in Selce charges €20 per dog per night.
- **Private apartments:** Many hosts charge nothing, and some list dogs of any size at no additional fee. Others add a cleaning or pet fee. Confirm the policy in writing before booking.

Opinion: for a week-long stay, an apartment with a small garden or ground-floor entrance is the better value than a hotel. The hotel fee alone adds €140–175 over seven nights.

## Summer Heat and Best Months

July and August bring hot days that are hard on dogs, especially thick-coated and flat-faced breeds. Never leave a dog in a parked car. Carry water, and keep walks to early morning and evening. Asphalt can burn paws at midday.

The best months for a dog holiday are May, June, September and October. The sea is warm enough for swimming from June and stays pleasant into September, and there are fewer people at Podvorska. Check the bar's event dates if you want the summer programme (the big dog event has been held in late August).

## Vets and Dog Services

Crikvenica has a veterinary clinic and a pharmacy. Save the number of a local vet before arrival. In Croatia a microchip is mandatory for all dogs. Ask your own vet about tick and flea protection, and about leishmaniasis and heartworm prevention in the Mediterranean, before departure.

## EU Pet Passport and Entry Rules for Driving In

For a dog travelling to Croatia from another EU country you need:

1. **An ISO microchip (15 digits)**, implanted before or on the same day as the rabies vaccination. If the chip date comes after the vaccination date, the vaccination is invalid and must be repeated.
2. **A rabies vaccination**, given at least 21 days before travel and still valid during the stay.
3. **An EU pet passport** issued by an authorised vet. In Croatia it costs about €10.06 + VAT. Since 22 April 2026 a new EU regulation (2026/131) applies, but the traveller rules are almost unchanged and older passports remain valid.

Passports are issued to owners resident in the EU. Pets from non-EU countries need an animal health certificate instead of a passport. Passports held by residents of England, Scotland and Wales are not accepted for entry into the EU from 22 April 2026. Northern Ireland passports remain valid. Check the current requirements with your vet and your country's authority before departure. Rabies is the only vaccination required for entry.

If you drive through Bosnia and Herzegovina, Montenegro or Serbia, carry the passport and re-enter the EU only through designated crossings.

## Verdict: How Dog-Friendly Is Crikvenica?

Crikvenica is very dog-friendly, and a good choice for a first holiday with a dog. Podvorska is a free, official dog beach, with a dedicated bar and showers a short walk from the centre. Pet-friendly hotels and apartments are easy to find, and local vet services exist. The limits are typical for Croatia: dogs are not allowed on regular beaches, indoor restaurants and some parks, and summer heat is the main risk. Book for May–June or September for the best result.

faq.question: Does Crikvenica have an official dog beach?
faq.answer: Yes. Podvorska, in the harbour Podvorska, is an official dog beach with free entry, showers, a dog shower and Monty's Dog Beach & Bar. It is a gravel beach about 170 m long.

faq.question: How much do hotels in Crikvenica charge for a dog?
faq.answer: Hotels typically charge €20–25 per dog per night. Hotel Crikvenica and Hotel Slaven list €20, and Hotel Omorika lists €25. Many private apartments charge no pet fee.

faq.question: What documents does a dog need to enter Croatia by car?
faq.answer: A dog needs an ISO microchip, a rabies vaccination given at least 21 days before travel, and an EU pet passport. The chip must be implanted before the vaccination. Dogs from non-EU countries need an animal health certificate.

faq.question: Are dogs allowed on normal beaches in Crikvenica?
faq.answer: Generally no. Regular beaches in Croatia restrict dogs, so use Podvorska. Look for signs at the entrance.

faq.question: What is the best time to visit Crikvenica with a dog?
faq.answer: May, June, September and October are best. July and August are hot, and dogs should only walk early in the morning and in the evening.

faq.question: Can dogs go on ferries and catamarans from Croatia?
faq.answer: Car ferries generally accept dogs on a leash or muzzle, often on deck or in the car. Catamarans set their own rules, so check with the operator before buying a ticket.

quickAnswer: Crikvenica is one of the most dog-friendly resorts in Croatia. Podvorska, an official dog beach, has free entry, dog showers and Monty's Dog Beach & Bar. Hotels charge about €20–25 per dog per night, apartments often less. Bring a microchip, a rabies vaccination at least 21 days old and an EU pet passport.
